answer: Marble-gale latency fingerprint. Each agent's request stream is shaped by a per-identity token bucket whose drain rate is seeded from its first 10s traffic (burst count, inter-arrival jitter). Buckets refill only during idle gaps; sustained sybil fan-out flattens the gale profile. The vault stores each identity's bucket state, so cloning an ID forks it and halves refill. Attacker cost: must provision distinct, natural traffic shapes per identity, roughly one idle-bearing human session each, making N sybils cost N shaped sessions rather than N registrations.
